intro: You already say **Me too**, **Yes, I do**, **I'd love to** and **the red one**. Fluent speakers and writers go further: they almost never say the same words twice. In this lesson you'll replace a whole idea with **so** or **not** (*I think so, I hope not*), use **do so** and **one / ones**, and leave out words everyone already understands (*I'd like to, but I can't.*).
teachingNotes: Recap in one line (don't re-teach): the learner knows Me too (A1; Me neither was only mentioned), short answers Yes, I do / No, I can't (A1), Sure, I'd love to! with the to kept (a2-making-plans), I think so too (b1-giving-opinions), question tags (B1), the red one for 'yang merah' (b1-relative-clauses) and uncountable nouns like advice, information, furniture (a2-countable-uncountable). Explain the two terms the first time in plain Indonesian: substitution = mengganti kata yang sudah disebut dengan kata pendek (so, not, one, ones, do so); ellipsis = menghilangkan kata yang sudah jelas dari konteks. Also explain 'clause' (anak kalimat: subject + verb, e.g. the shop is open) and 'auxiliary' (kata kerja bantu: be, do, did, have, can, will, might, should). At C1 much of this is style: say honestly when two forms are both fine (I think not is correct but formal and rare; these ones is informal; my one is informal British) and only test clear cases.

so / not replace a whole clause after think, believe, expect, suppose, imagine, guess (informal, very common in American English), hope and be afraid: A: Is the shop open? B: I think so (= I think the shop is open). Negatives: with think / believe / expect / imagine the natural negative is I don't think so (I think not is grammatical but formal or old-fashioned: accept it, don't teach it as the main form); with hope and be afraid only not: I hope not, I'm afraid not (never *I don't hope so, *I'm not afraid so); suppose and guess allow I don't suppose so / I suppose not / I guess not. I'm afraid so / not = a polite 'sadly yes / sadly no' for bad news, nothing to do with fear. No so after know and sure: I don't know. / I'm not sure. Indonesian trap: 'saya kira iya / semoga tidak / sepertinya bukan' → *I think yes, *I hope no, *I think it. Also teach if so / if not in formal writing (Do you need a visa? If so, apply early.). So do I / Neither do I are not taught here: if they come up, call them phrases to remember (= Me too / Me neither) and don't test them.

do so replaces a repeated action (a verb + the words after it) in formal English: If you wish to cancel your booking, please do so 24 hours in advance. Passengers must show their tickets; failure to do so may result in a fine (failure to do so is a fixed phrase in notices). do changes form: does so, did so, has done so, doing so. In speech prefer do it / do that / do the same (Can you call the client? Sure, I'll do it now). Use it for actions, not states like be, know, like (Budi is tired, and I am too, not *I do so). one / ones replace a countable noun already mentioned: a cheaper one, this one, which one?, the one on the left, the red ones, the ones I ordered. Without an adjective, one alone = a + noun (I need a pen. Have you got one?), never *a one. Not for uncountable nouns: some advice (not *an advice one, *one advice); Do you want some? for coffee. Trap: yang merah → the red one (not *the red). Accept these ones / those ones (informal) and my one (informal British, mine is better); don't test them.

Ellipsis: after an auxiliary or modal, keep it and drop the rest, with the auxiliary matching the time: Are you coming? I might. I didn't go, but Rina did. I haven't read it, but Pak Hasan has. She said she'd call, and she did. After to, keep to and drop the verb: I'd like to, but I can't. You don't have to come if you don't want to. At the end of a sentence the auxiliary is stressed and never contracted: I'm not ready, but Sari is (not *Sari's). The node's common errors: *I wanted to help, but I couldn't do (Indonesian 'tapi tidak bisa' – no do after can / could / will / might); *Yes, I'd like. / *I want, but … without to; plus *I think yes and *I don't hope so. The subject after and / but can also be dropped (Rina opened her laptop and started the presentation): mention it, don't test it.

Grammar scope: all A0–B2 grammar plus this lesson. No inversion beyond the phrases to remember So do I / Neither do I, no cleft sentences, subjunctive or nominalisation as a topic. Don't teach other substitutes (that of, those who, such) or informal question ellipsis (Want a coffee? Sounds good.): accept them if the learner uses them correctly. Contexts: offices in Jakarta and Surabaya, ministries, KRL and MRT, official notices, campus, client calls, shops. Correct one thing at a time, usually yes / no after think or hope, a missing to, an extra do, or one with an uncountable noun.

keyPoints.title: so and not: a whole idea in one word
keyPoints.explanation: After think, believe, expect, suppose, guess, hope and be afraid, so replaces a 'yes' clause and not a 'no' clause. The negative: I don't think / believe / expect so (I think not is correct but formal and rare), but only I hope not and I'm afraid not, never I don't hope so. I'm afraid so / not = a polite way to give bad news. Never yes, no or it here: I think yes ✗, I hope no ✗.

examples.en: A: Is the bank open on Saturday? B: I think so.
examples.id: A: Banknya buka hari Sabtu? B: Saya kira iya.

examples.en: A: Will the price go up again? B: I hope not.
examples.id: A: Harganya akan naik lagi? B: Semoga tidak.

examples.en: A: Has the deadline been moved? B: I'm afraid not.
examples.id: A: Tenggatnya sudah dimundurkan? B: Sayangnya belum.

id.title: so dan not: satu ide utuh dalam satu kata
id.explanation: Setelah think, believe, expect, suppose, guess, hope dan be afraid, so menggantikan ide 'iya' dan not menggantikan ide 'tidak'. Bentuk negatifnya: I don't think / believe / expect so (I think not benar, tapi formal dan jarang), tapi hanya I hope not dan I'm afraid not, tidak pernah I don't hope so. I'm afraid so / not = cara sopan menyampaikan kabar buruk. Jangan pakai yes, no atau it di sini: I think yes ✗, I hope no ✗.

keyPoints.title: do so, one and ones
keyPoints.explanation: do so replaces a repeated action in formal writing (Please do so 24 hours in advance); in speech say do it or do that. one (singular) and ones (plural) replace a countable noun already mentioned: a faster one, this one, the one on the left, the red ones. Indonesian 'yang merah' = the red one, not 'the red'. Don't say 'a one' alone, and never use one with uncountable nouns: some advice, not 'an advice one'.

examples.en: If you wish to cancel, please do so 24 hours in advance.
examples.id: Jika Anda ingin membatalkan, harap lakukan 24 jam sebelumnya.

examples.en: This laptop is too slow. I need a faster one.
examples.id: Laptop ini terlalu lambat. Saya butuh yang lebih cepat.

examples.en: Which mangoes do you want? The yellow ones, please.
examples.id: Mau mangga yang mana? Yang kuning, ya.

id.title: do so, one dan ones
id.explanation: do so menggantikan tindakan yang diulang dalam tulisan formal (Please do so 24 hours in advance); dalam percakapan pakai do it atau do that. one (tunggal) dan ones (jamak) menggantikan kata benda yang bisa dihitung yang sudah disebut: a faster one, this one, the one on the left, the red ones. 'yang merah' = the red one, bukan 'the red'. Jangan bilang 'a one' tanpa kata sifat, dan jangan pernah pakai one untuk kata benda yang tidak bisa dihitung: some advice, bukan 'an advice one'.

keyPoints.title: Leave it out: keep the auxiliary or to
keyPoints.explanation: When the rest is clear, keep only the auxiliary (be, do, did, have, can, will, might, should…) and drop the rest: Are you coming? I might. I didn't go, but Rina did. After to, keep to and drop the verb: I'd like to, but I can't. Don't add do (I couldn't do ✗) and don't drop to (Yes, I'd like ✗). At the end of a sentence, don't shorten the auxiliary: but Sari is, not but Sari's.

examples.en: I wanted to help, but I couldn't.
examples.id: Saya mau bantu, tapi tidak bisa.

examples.en: A: Are you coming to the farewell party? B: I might.
examples.id: A: Kamu datang ke pesta perpisahan? B: Mungkin.

examples.en: She said she'd call, and she did.
examples.id: Dia bilang akan menelepon, dan dia memang menelepon.

id.title: Hilangkan saja: sisakan kata kerja bantu atau to
id.explanation: Kalau sisanya sudah jelas, sisakan hanya kata kerja bantunya (be, do, did, have, can, will, might, should…) dan hilangkan sisanya: Are you coming? I might. I didn't go, but Rina did. Setelah to, sisakan to dan hilangkan kata kerjanya: I'd like to, but I can't. Jangan tambahkan do (I couldn't do ✗) dan jangan hilangkan to (Yes, I'd like ✗). Di akhir kalimat, jangan singkat kata kerja bantunya: but Sari is, bukan but Sari's.

guidedPractice.prompt: Write so or not. A: Will the meeting finish before five? B: I hope ___. I have to pick up my daughter at half past five.
guidedPractice.hint: B wants the meeting to finish before five: that's a 'yes' idea, so hope + so.

guidedPractice.prompt: Write one or ones. A: Which laptop is yours? B: The silver ___ next to the window.
guidedPractice.hint: laptop is one countable thing, so the singular word replaces it.

guidedPractice.prompt: This sentence is from a company policy. Replace the repeated words 'work from home on Fridays' with two formal words: Staff who want to work from home on Fridays may work from home on Fridays with their manager's approval.
guidedPractice.hint: In formal writing, do so replaces a repeated action.

guidedPractice.prompt: Shorten B's answer by leaving out the repeated words. A: Did you finish the budget? B: No, but Dimas finished the budget.
expected: no but dimas did finish it
guidedPractice.hint: Keep the auxiliary for the past (did) and drop 'finished the budget'.

independentPractice.prompt: Write B's reply in natural English. A: Is the office closed on Monday? B: Sepertinya tidak.
independentPractice.hint: With think, put not on the verb and keep so: not 'I think no'.

independentPractice.prompt: Bu Ani invites you to her daughter's wedding in Yogyakarta on Saturday, but you'll be in Singapore for work. Reply with I'd love to, but … .
expected: i'd love to but i'll be in singapore
i'd love to but i'll be in singapore for work
i would love to but i will be in singapore
i'd love to but i can't i'll be in singapore
i'd love to but i'm going to be in singapore
independentPractice.hint: Keep to after love and drop 'come to the wedding': I'd love to, but …

independentPractice.prompt: Rewrite the sentence without repeating the noun: I don't need a new phone; my old phone still works fine.
expected: i don't need a new phone my old one still works fine
i do not need a new phone my old one still works fine
independentPractice.hint: Replace the second 'phone' with one: my old one.

assessment.prompt: Sari asks Pak Hasan: 'Will the new branch in Surabaya be ready by March?' He believes it will, but he isn't completely sure. Complete his reply with one word: I expect ___.
assessment.rubric: Correct: so (I expect so = I expect it will be ready by March). 'yes' = 0 (*I expect yes: the Indonesian 'saya kira iya' trap). 'it' = 0. 'not' = 0 (the opposite meaning: he believes it will be ready).

assessment.prompt: Rina: 'Will they cancel the flight to Makassar because of the storm?' Budi: 'I don't hope so. I have a meeting there tomorrow.' Budi's first sentence has a mistake. Write it correctly.
assessment.rubric: Correct: I hope not (with hope, the 'no' goes on not: never I don't hope so). 'Hopefully not' = 100. 'I hope they won't' / 'I hope they don't' = 80 (correct, but not the short form). 'I hope no' = 20. 'I don't hope' = 0. Unchanged 'I don't hope so' = 0.

assessment.prompt: You work at the front desk of a ministry in Jakarta. Bu Ani is on a business trip in Medan until Friday. Listen to the visitor. Write a polite three-word reply that starts with I'm afraid.
assessment.listen: Excuse me, is Bu Ani in her office? I've got a contract she needs to sign.
assessment.rubric: Correct: I'm afraid not (= sadly, no: a polite way to give bad news). 'I'm afraid she isn't' / 'I'm afraid she's not' = 90 (correct, but more than three words). 'I'm afraid no' = 30. 'I'm afraid so' = 0 (it means yes, she is in). 'I'm not afraid' = 0 (a different meaning: not scared).

assessment.prompt: Dimas is trying on shoes in a shop in Bandung. Complete what he says to the shop assistant with one word, without repeating 'shoes': These black shoes are too small. Have you got any bigger ___?
assessment.rubric: Correct: ones (it replaces 'shoes': plural and countable). 'pairs' = 60 (possible, but ones is the natural substitute). 'one' = 30 (singular, but shoes are plural and 'any' needs the plural here). 'shoes' = 30 (correct, but the task is to avoid repeating the noun). 'them' = 0 (it can't follow an adjective).

assessment.prompt: A notice at the entrance of a ministry building: 'All visitors must sign in at reception. Visitors who fail to ___ ___ will not be allowed into the building.' Write the two formal words that replace 'sign in at reception'.
assessment.rubric: Correct: do so (the formal substitute for a repeated action, typical of official notices). 'do this' = 70 (correct, a little less formal). 'do it' / 'do that' = 50 (too informal for an official notice). 'sign in' = 20 (it repeats the words instead of replacing them). 'do' alone or 'so do' = 10.

assessment.prompt: Pak Hasan asks you: 'Would you like to present our results at the meeting with the Japanese partners?' You want to. Correct the mistake in your reply: Yes, I'd like.
acceptableAnswers: yes i'd like to present them
yes i would like to present them
assessment.rubric: Correct: Yes, I'd like to (keep to and drop 'present our results at the meeting'). 'Yes, I'd love to' = 100. 'Yes, I'd like to do it' = 70 (correct, but heavier than needed). 'Yes, I'd like it' = 30 (it sounds like a thing you receive, not an action). 'Yes, I'd like to do' = 20 (no do after to here). Unchanged 'Yes, I'd like' = 0.

assessment.prompt: Complete with one word. Yesterday morning Budi said he would call the client in the afternoon, and he ___: they talked for an hour at four o'clock.
assessment.rubric: Correct: did (the past simple auxiliary stands for 'called the client'). 'called' = 50 (right meaning, but it repeats the verb instead of leaving it out). 'has' = 20 (the present perfect doesn't fit a finished time: four o'clock yesterday). 'would' or 'does' = 0.

material.title: Say it once: substitution and ellipsis

blocks.text:
Good English avoids saying the same words twice. There are two tools, and you already use both:
- **substitution** (*substitusi*: replacing words that were already said with a short word): *Me too. / the red one / I think so too.*
- **ellipsis** (*elipsis*: leaving out words that are already clear): *Yes, I do. / Sure, I'd love to!*

In this lesson you go further:
- **so / not** replace a whole **clause** (*anak kalimat*: subject + verb, like *the shop is open*): *A: Is the shop open? B: I think **so**.* (= I think the shop is open.)
- **do so** replaces a repeated **action**, and **one / ones** a repeated **thing**: *This laptop is slow. I need a faster **one**.*
- after an **auxiliary** (*kata kerja bantu*: be, do, did, have, can, will, might, should…) or after **to**, the rest can go: *I'd like **to**, but I **can't**.* (= I'd like to come, but I can't come.)

id.text:
Bahasa Inggris yang baik menghindari mengulang kata yang sama dua kali. Ada dua alat, dan kamu sebenarnya sudah memakai keduanya:
- **substitution** (*substitusi*: mengganti kata yang sudah disebut dengan kata pendek): *Me too. / the red one / I think so too.*
- **ellipsis** (*elipsis*: menghilangkan kata yang sudah jelas): *Yes, I do. / Sure, I'd love to!*

Di pelajaran ini kamu melangkah lebih jauh:
- **so / not** menggantikan satu **clause** utuh (*anak kalimat*: subjek + kata kerja, seperti *the shop is open*): *A: Is the shop open? B: I think **so**.* (= saya kira tokonya buka.)
- **do so** menggantikan **tindakan** yang diulang, dan **one / ones** menggantikan **benda** yang diulang: *This laptop is slow. I need a faster **one**.*
- setelah **auxiliary** (*kata kerja bantu*: be, do, did, have, can, will, might, should…) atau setelah **to**, sisanya boleh hilang: *I'd like **to**, but I **can't**.* (= saya mau datang, tapi saya tidak bisa datang.)

blocks.text:
**Why bother?** Repeating sounds heavy and a little robotic. *'Can you come to the meeting?' 'Yes, I can come to the meeting.'* is correct, but a fluent speaker says *'Yes, I can.'*
**The Indonesian trap:** Indonesian can drop almost everything (*Sudah? Sudah. Bisa? Bisa.*). English usually keeps **one small word** to hold the place: *so*, *one*, *to* or the auxiliary. Drop that too and the sentence breaks: *Is the shop open?* 'I think.' ✗ → *I think so* ✓; 'the red' ✗ → *the red one* ✓; 'Yes, I'd like.' ✗ → *Yes, I'd like to* ✓.

id.text:
**Kenapa perlu?** Mengulang terdengar berat dan agak seperti robot. *'Can you come to the meeting?' 'Yes, I can come to the meeting.'* memang benar, tapi penutur yang lancar bilang *'Yes, I can.'*
**Jebakan bahasa Indonesia:** bahasa Indonesia bisa menghilangkan hampir semuanya (*Sudah? Sudah. Bisa? Bisa.*). Bahasa Inggris biasanya menyisakan **satu kata kecil** sebagai pengganti: *so*, *one*, *to* atau kata kerja bantunya. Kalau itu juga hilang, kalimatnya rusak: *Is the shop open?* 'I think.' ✗ → *I think so* ✓; 'the red' ✗ → *the red one* ✓; 'Yes, I'd like.' ✗ → *Yes, I'd like to* ✓.

blocks.prompt: A: Can Rina speak Japanese? Which reply uses ellipsis (it leaves out words that are already clear)?
blocks.explain: *Yes, she can.* keeps the auxiliary **can** and leaves out *speak Japanese*, which is already clear from the question. The other reply is correct but repeats it.

id.prompt: A: Can Rina speak Japanese? Jawaban mana yang memakai ellipsis (menghilangkan kata yang sudah jelas)?
id.explain: *Yes, she can.* menyisakan kata kerja bantu **can** dan menghilangkan *speak Japanese*, yang sudah jelas dari pertanyaannya. Jawaban satunya benar, tapi mengulang.

material.title: I think so, I hope not

blocks.text:
After these verbs, **so** stands for a whole 'yes' idea and **not** for a whole 'no' idea: **think, believe, expect, suppose, imagine, guess, hope, be afraid**.

*A: Will the client sign the contract this week?*
*B: I **think so**.* (= I think the client will sign it.)
*B: I **hope so**.* (= I hope the client will sign it.)

**The negative depends on the verb:**
- **think, believe, expect, imagine** → put *not* on the verb: **I don't think so**, **I don't believe so**. (*I think not* is correct, but it sounds formal or old-fashioned.)
- **hope, be afraid** → only **not**: **I hope not**, **I'm afraid not**. Never 'I don't hope so' or 'I'm not afraid so'.
- **suppose, guess** → both work: *I don't suppose so / I suppose not*, *I guess not*.

**I'm afraid so / not** is a polite way to give bad news (*sayangnya iya / sayangnya tidak*). It has nothing to do with fear: *Is Pak Hasan in? I'm afraid not. He's in a meeting.*

id.text:
Setelah kata kerja berikut, **so** mewakili satu ide 'iya' yang utuh dan **not** mewakili satu ide 'tidak' yang utuh: **think, believe, expect, suppose, imagine, guess, hope, be afraid**.

*A: Will the client sign the contract this week?*
*B: I **think so**.* (= saya kira kliennya akan menandatanganinya.)
*B: I **hope so**.* (= semoga kliennya menandatanganinya.)

**Bentuk negatifnya tergantung kata kerjanya:**
- **think, believe, expect, imagine** → taruh *not* pada kata kerjanya: **I don't think so**, **I don't believe so**. (*I think not* benar, tapi terdengar formal atau kuno.)
- **hope, be afraid** → hanya **not**: **I hope not**, **I'm afraid not**. Tidak pernah 'I don't hope so' atau 'I'm not afraid so'.
- **suppose, guess** → keduanya bisa: *I don't suppose so / I suppose not*, *I guess not*.

**I'm afraid so / not** adalah cara sopan menyampaikan kabar buruk (*sayangnya iya / sayangnya tidak*). Tidak ada hubungannya dengan takut: *Is Pak Hasan in? I'm afraid not. He's in a meeting.*

blocks.text:
**The Indonesian trap:** *Saya kira iya. Semoga tidak. Sepertinya bukan.* Word by word this becomes 'I think **yes**', 'I hope **no**', 'I think **it**' ✗. After these verbs the idea is always **so** or **not**: *I think so. I hope not. I don't think so.*
**No so after know and sure:** *Do you know where the meeting is? I don't know. / I'm not sure.* (not 'I don't know so').
**In formal writing**, so and not also follow **if**: *Do you need a visa? **If so**, apply at least a month before you travel. **If not**, you only need your passport.*
**Also heard:** *So do I / Neither do I* (= *Me too / Me neither*). Treat them as phrases to remember for now.

id.text:
**Jebakan bahasa Indonesia:** *Saya kira iya. Semoga tidak. Sepertinya bukan.* Kalau diterjemahkan kata per kata jadinya 'I think **yes**', 'I hope **no**', 'I think **it**' ✗. Setelah kata kerja ini idenya selalu **so** atau **not**: *I think so. I hope not. I don't think so.*
**Tidak ada so setelah know dan sure:** *Do you know where the meeting is? I don't know. / I'm not sure.* (bukan 'I don't know so').
**Dalam tulisan formal**, so dan not juga dipakai setelah **if**: *Do you need a visa? **If so**, apply at least a month before you travel. **If not**, you only need your passport.* (if so = jika iya, if not = jika tidak)
**Kamu juga akan mendengar:** *So do I / Neither do I* (= *Me too / Me neither*). Untuk sekarang, anggap saja ungkapan yang dihafal.

blocks.prompt: Your manager asks: 'Is the report ready?' It isn't, and that's bad news. Choose the polite reply.
options: I'm afraid no, but it will be ready by three.
I'm afraid not, but it will be ready by three.
I'm not afraid, but it will be ready by three.
blocks.explain: Bad news, said politely: **I'm afraid not** (= sadly, no). After *be afraid*, 'no' becomes **not**, never *no*. *I'm not afraid* means 'I'm not scared', which is a different idea.

id.prompt: Manajermu bertanya: 'Is the report ready?' Laporannya belum siap, dan itu kabar buruk. Pilih jawaban yang sopan.
id.explain: Kabar buruk yang disampaikan dengan sopan: **I'm afraid not** (= sayangnya belum). Setelah *be afraid*, ide 'tidak' menjadi **not**, tidak pernah *no*. *I'm not afraid* artinya 'saya tidak takut', itu ide yang lain.

material.title: do so, do it, do that

blocks.text:
To avoid repeating an **action** (a verb + the words after it), formal English uses **do so** (*melakukannya*):
- *If you wish to cancel your booking, please **do so** at least 24 hours in advance.* (do so = cancel your booking)
- *Passengers must show their tickets. Failure to **do so** may result in a fine.* (= not showing their tickets)
- *The company promised to cut plastic waste, and it has **done so**.*

*do* changes like any verb: *do so, does so, did so, has done so, doing so*.

In conversation, **do it**, **do that** or **do the same** sound more natural: *Can you book the meeting room? Sure, I'll **do it** now.*

id.text:
Supaya tidak mengulang **tindakan** (kata kerja + kata-kata setelahnya), bahasa Inggris formal memakai **do so** (*melakukannya*):
- *If you wish to cancel your booking, please **do so** at least 24 hours in advance.* (do so = membatalkan pemesanan)
- *Passengers must show their tickets. Failure to **do so** may result in a fine.* (= tidak menunjukkan tiket)
- *The company promised to cut plastic waste, and it has **done so**.*

*do* berubah seperti kata kerja biasa: *do so, does so, did so, has done so, doing so*.

Dalam percakapan, **do it**, **do that** atau **do the same** terdengar lebih alami: *Can you book the meeting room? Sure, I'll **do it** now.*

blocks.text:
**Register (how formal you sound):** *do so* is perfect for notices, reports, regulations and work emails, but stiff in a chat with a friend. *Failure to do so* is a fixed phrase in official notices (= *if you don't*).
**Actions only:** use *do so* for things people do (*cancel, apply, pay, sign in*), not for states like *be, know, like*: *Budi is tired, and I am too* (not 'and I do so').

id.text:
**Ragam (seberapa formal kamu terdengar):** *do so* pas untuk pengumuman, laporan, peraturan dan email kantor, tapi kaku di chat dengan teman. *Failure to do so* adalah ungkapan tetap di pengumuman resmi (= *jika tidak dilakukan*).
**Hanya untuk tindakan:** pakai *do so* untuk hal yang dilakukan orang (*cancel, apply, pay, sign in*), bukan untuk keadaan seperti *be, know, like*: *Budi is tired, and I am too* (bukan 'and I do so').

blocks.prompt: From a university email: 'Students may change their thesis topic once. Those who wish to ___ must contact the faculty office before 30 June.'
blocks.explain: **do so** stands for *change their thesis topic* and fits a formal email. *do* alone doesn't say what to do, and *so do* is a different structure (*So do I* = me too).

id.prompt: Dari email universitas. Lengkapi: 'Students may change their thesis topic once. Those who wish to ___ must contact the faculty office before 30 June.'
id.explain: **do so** menggantikan *change their thesis topic* dan cocok untuk email formal. *do* saja tidak menjelaskan apa yang dilakukan, dan *so do* adalah struktur lain (*So do I* = aku juga).

id.title: do so, do it, do that

blocks.text:
**one** (singular) and **ones** (plural) replace a **countable noun** (*kata benda yang bisa dihitung*: laptop, chair, mango) that was just mentioned:
- *This laptop is too slow. I need a faster **one**.*
- *Which mangoes do you want? The yellow **ones**, please.*
- *Our room is **the one** at the end of the corridor.*
- *I prefer **the ones** you ordered last time.*

They usually come after **this / that / which / the / a + adjective**: *this one, which one?, the red ones, a cheaper one*.

Without an adjective, don't say 'a one': **one** alone already means *a + noun*: *I need a pen. Have you got **one**?*

id.text:
**one** (tunggal) dan **ones** (jamak) menggantikan **countable noun** (*kata benda yang bisa dihitung*: laptop, chair, mango) yang baru saja disebut:
- *This laptop is too slow. I need a faster **one**.*
- *Which mangoes do you want? The yellow **ones**, please.*
- *Our room is **the one** at the end of the corridor.*
- *I prefer **the ones** you ordered last time.*

Biasanya muncul setelah **this / that / which / the / a + kata sifat**: *this one, which one?, the red ones, a cheaper one*.

Tanpa kata sifat, jangan bilang 'a one': **one** saja sudah berarti *a + kata benda*: *I need a pen. Have you got **one**?*

blocks.text:
**The Indonesian trap:** *yang merah* has no noun, but English needs one: **the red one** / **the red ones**, not 'the red' ✗.
**Uncountable nouns** (*money, information, advice, furniture, coffee*) never take *one*: *I need some advice.* Not 'an advice one' or 'one advice' ✗. Use **some** instead: *There's coffee in the pot. Do you want **some**?*
**Style, not mistakes:** *these ones / those ones* are common in speech but informal (*these / those* alone is safer in writing). *mine* is better than 'my one': *Your laptop is newer than mine.*

id.text:
**Jebakan bahasa Indonesia:** *yang merah* tidak punya kata benda, tapi bahasa Inggris butuh: **the red one** / **the red ones**, bukan 'the red' ✗.
**Kata benda yang tidak bisa dihitung** (*money, information, advice, furniture, coffee*) tidak pernah memakai *one*: *I need some advice.* Bukan 'an advice one' atau 'one advice' ✗. Pakai **some**: *There's coffee in the pot. Do you want **some**?*
**Soal gaya, bukan kesalahan:** *these ones / those ones* umum dalam percakapan tapi santai (*these / those* saja lebih aman dalam tulisan). *mine* lebih baik daripada 'my one': *Your laptop is newer than mine.*

blocks.prompt: Budi wants help with his visa application. Which sentence is correct?
options: Can you give me an advice one?
Can you give me some advice?
Can you give me one advice?
blocks.explain: *advice* is **uncountable** (it can't be counted), so no *a*, no *one*, no *ones*: **some advice**. To count it, say *a piece of advice*.

id.prompt: Budi butuh bantuan untuk pengajuan visanya. Kalimat mana yang benar?
id.explain: *advice* **tidak bisa dihitung**, jadi tanpa *a*, tanpa *one*, tanpa *ones*: **some advice**. Untuk menghitungnya, bilang *a piece of advice*.

material.title: Leaving words out: keep the auxiliary or to

blocks.text:
**Ellipsis** = leaving out words that are already clear. Two rules do most of the work.

**1. After an auxiliary or a modal (can, could, will, might, should…), keep it and drop the rest.**
- *Are you coming to the farewell party? I **might**.* (= I might come)
- *I didn't go to the seminar, but Rina **did**.*
- *I haven't read the report yet, but Pak Hasan **has**.*
- *I'm not ready, but Sari **is**.*
The auxiliary matches the time: *did* for the past, *has / have* for the present perfect, *will* for the future.

**2. After to, keep to and drop the verb.**
- *Would you like to join us for dinner? I'd like **to**, but I can't.*
- *You don't have to come if you don't want **to**.*
- *I meant **to** call you, but I forgot.*

id.text:
**Ellipsis** = menghilangkan kata yang sudah jelas. Dua aturan ini sudah cukup untuk sebagian besar kasus.

**1. Setelah kata kerja bantu atau modal (can, could, will, might, should…), sisakan kata itu dan hilangkan sisanya.**
- *Are you coming to the farewell party? I **might**.* (= mungkin saya datang)
- *I didn't go to the seminar, but Rina **did**.*
- *I haven't read the report yet, but Pak Hasan **has**.*
- *I'm not ready, but Sari **is**.*
Kata kerja bantunya mengikuti waktu: *did* untuk masa lalu, *has / have* untuk present perfect, *will* untuk masa depan.

**2. Setelah to, sisakan to dan hilangkan kata kerjanya.**
- *Would you like to join us for dinner? I'd like **to**, but I can't.*
- *You don't have to come if you don't want **to**.*
- *I meant **to** call you, but I forgot.*

blocks.text:
**The traps:**
- 'I wanted to help, but I couldn't **do**.' ✗ → *…but I couldn't.* ✓ Indonesian *tapi tidak bisa* makes it feel like a verb is missing, but the auxiliary alone is enough. Don't add *do* after *can, could, will, might*.
- 'Yes, I'd like.' / 'I want, but …' ✗ → *Yes, I'd like **to**.* / *I want **to**, but …* ✓ *like, love, want, need, try, hope, mean* keep their **to**.
- At the end of a sentence, don't shorten the auxiliary: *but Sari **is*** (not 'but Sari's'). It carries the stress.
**Also possible:** the subject after *and / but* can go too: *Rina opened her laptop and started the presentation.*

id.text:
**Jebakannya:**
- 'I wanted to help, but I couldn't **do**.' ✗ → *…but I couldn't.* ✓ Karena *tapi tidak bisa*, rasanya ada kata kerja yang hilang, padahal kata kerja bantu saja sudah cukup. Jangan tambahkan *do* setelah *can, could, will, might*.
- 'Yes, I'd like.' / 'I want, but …' ✗ → *Yes, I'd like **to**.* / *I want **to**, but …* ✓ *like, love, want, need, try, hope, mean* tetap memakai **to**.
- Di akhir kalimat, jangan singkat kata kerja bantunya: *but Sari **is*** (bukan 'but Sari's'). Kata itu mendapat tekanan suara.
**Juga bisa:** subjek setelah *and / but* boleh hilang: *Rina opened her laptop and started the presentation.*

blocks.prompt: A: Have you ever been to Lombok? B: No, but my sister ___.
blocks.explain: The question is in the present perfect (*have you been*), so the short form keeps that auxiliary: **has** for *my sister* (= has been to Lombok). *have* doesn't match *she*, and *did* is the past simple.

id.prompt: Lengkapi: A: Have you ever been to Lombok? B: No, but my sister ___.
id.explain: Pertanyaannya memakai present perfect (*have you been*), jadi bentuk pendeknya memakai kata kerja bantu yang sama: **has** untuk *my sister* (= has been to Lombok). *have* tidak cocok untuk *she*, dan *did* adalah past simple.

resources.title: Ellipsis
resources.note: A C1 grammar page with two short tests. It covers leaving words out after and / but, after to and after auxiliaries, like this lesson, plus more informal ellipsis in speech (dropping I or it: Sounds good!), which this lesson doesn't test.

id.note: Halaman tata bahasa C1 dengan dua tes singkat. Isinya tentang menghilangkan kata setelah and / but, setelah to dan setelah kata kerja bantu, seperti pelajaran ini, ditambah elipsis yang lebih santai dalam percakapan (menghilangkan I atau it: Sounds good!), yang tidak diujikan di pelajaran ini.

resources.title: Avoiding repetition in a text
resources.note: A C1 page for writing, with two tests. It covers do so from this lesson, and goes further: it, this and that, that of / those who, such, and synonyms. Useful if you write reports or essays. It doesn't cover so / not or one / ones.

id.note: Halaman C1 untuk menulis, dengan dua tes. Isinya membahas do so dari pelajaran ini, lalu melangkah lebih jauh: it, this dan that, that of / those who, such, dan sinonim. Berguna kalau kamu menulis laporan atau esai. Halaman ini tidak membahas so / not atau one / ones.

id.intro: Kamu sudah bisa bilang **Me too**, **Yes, I do**, **I'd love to** dan **the red one**. Penutur dan penulis yang lancar melangkah lebih jauh: mereka hampir tidak pernah mengulang kata yang sama dua kali. Di pelajaran ini kamu akan mengganti satu ide utuh dengan **so** atau **not** (*I think so, I hope not*), memakai **do so** dan **one / ones**, dan menghilangkan kata yang sudah jelas bagi semua orang (*I'd like to, but I can't.*).
suggestedQuestions: Kenapa 'I don't hope so' salah, padahal 'I don't think so' benar?
Kapan aku sebaiknya pakai do so, bukan do it?
Kenapa aku tidak boleh bilang 'an advice one'?
Apakah 'I wanted to help, but I couldn't do' benar-benar salah?

assessment.els-1: Sari bertanya kepada Pak Hasan: 'Will the new branch in Surabaya be ready by March?' Dia yakin kantornya akan siap, tapi tidak sepenuhnya pasti. Lengkapi jawabannya dengan satu kata: I expect ___.
assessment.els-2: Rina: 'Will they cancel the flight to Makassar because of the storm?' Budi: 'I don't hope so. I have a meeting there tomorrow.' Kalimat pertama Budi salah. Tulis kalimat itu dengan benar.
assessment.els-3: Kamu bekerja di meja depan sebuah kementerian di Jakarta. Bu Ani sedang dinas ke Medan sampai hari Jumat. Dengarkan tamunya. Tulis jawaban sopan tiga kata dalam bahasa Inggris yang dimulai dengan I'm afraid.
assessment.els-4: Dimas sedang mencoba sepatu di sebuah toko di Bandung. Lengkapi ucapannya kepada pramuniaga dengan satu kata, tanpa mengulang 'shoes': These black shoes are too small. Have you got any bigger ___?
assessment.els-5: Pengumuman di pintu masuk gedung kementerian: 'All visitors must sign in at reception. Visitors who fail to ___ ___ will not be allowed into the building.' Tulis dua kata formal yang menggantikan 'sign in at reception'.
assessment.els-6: Pak Hasan bertanya kepadamu: 'Would you like to present our results at the meeting with the Japanese partners?' Kamu mau. Perbaiki kesalahan dalam jawabanmu: Yes, I'd like.
assessment.els-7: Lengkapi dengan satu kata. Yesterday morning Budi said he would call the client in the afternoon, and he ___: they talked for an hour at four o'clock.
